newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian philosopher Fernard Dumont dies at 69.
newsitem.headline: Canadian philosopher Fernard Dumont dies at 69.

text.p: One of Canada's most renowned philosopher died early Friday following a long and painful cancer.

Fernard Dumont, 69, a poet, humanist, sociologist and philosopher was a sociology teacher at Quebec City's Laval University and director of Quebec's Institute of Research on culture from 1980 to 1990. An erudite and a catholic, Dumont was deputy-director of the Ecole des Hautes Etudes in Paris in the 1960s and president from 1975 to 1978 of the International Association of French-language sociologists.

Dumont, who wrote mainly sociological essays and books on the psyche of the Canadian French-speaking province of 7.1 million inhabitants, is the author of the Charter of the French Language, a legislation tabled in 1977 by the separatist government of Rene Levesque that made French the official language in Quebec and prohibited the use of English in commercial signs. Dumont is also known for helping writing the legislation on Quebec separation before the October 1995 referendum.
Dumont received Canada's Governor-General Award for litterature in 1969 and was a Doctor honoris causa from Paris' Sorbonne University.

Born in Montmorency, Quebec in 1927, Dumont did his Bachelor's degree at the University of Paris and his Master's degree in humanities at Laval University. He got a Doctorate's degree in sociology from Sorbonne University and in theology at Laval University.
